entities.name: Demetrius of Thessaloniki
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Demetrius of Thessaloniki, the Holy Great-Martyr Demetrius the Myroblyte, was a Greek Christian martyr of the early 4th century AD.

Born around 290 CE in Thessalonica, a major city in the Roman province of Macedonia, Demetrius was a prominent figure in the Christian community.

In 306 CE, during the reign of Emperor Diocletian, Demetrius was arrested, tortured, and eventually executed for his faith. His martyrdom at the hand of the Roman prefect of Thessalonica, Sisinnius, marked a significant turning point in the early Christian movement.

Demetrius' legacy extends beyond his own time, as his cult of saints spread throughout the Eastern Roman Empire and later to the Byzantine Empire. His feast day, September 26, is still celebrated by the Orthodox Church today.

The Demetrius of Thessaloniki's story serves as a powerful testament to the enduring power of faith and the human spirit in the face of persecution.
